title: Gospel of Matthew
author: matthew-evangelist
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Matthew the Evangelist. Most modern scholars regard the Gospel as anonymous and composed by a later author using Mark and other traditions.
description: The Gospel of Matthew presents Jesus as a teacher and fulfilments of Israel's scriptures. The Sermon on the Mount opens with the Beatitudes, a compact portrait of the life the Gospel commends.
historicalContext: Matthew was likely written after the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple (70 CE), in a community negotiating its relationship with Judaism and the wider Greco-Roman world.
featuredNote: The Beatitudes and the ethics of mercy

chapters.label: Chapter 5 — the Sermon on the Mount

editions.title: The Holy Bible, King James Version
editions.attributionText: The Holy Bible, King James Version (1611). Public domain. Text from Project Gutenberg eBook #10.
editions.notes: Demonstration edition contains English only. A Greek original for Matthew is not yet included in the corpus; the work record still identifies Greek as its original language.

texts.5.3: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
texts.5.4: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
texts.5.5: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
texts.5.6: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
texts.5.7: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
texts.5.8: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
texts.5.9: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
texts.5.10: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
texts.5.11: Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
texts.5.12: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.
